---
title: "CMS Start cutover packet"
description: "Source and operator checklist for a future CMS Worker cutover."
updatedAt: "2026-11-24"
audience: developers
---

CMS has a TanStack Start/Void candidate. Production publication and routing are
held; this packet records the source target and checks required before Rex
authorizes a cutover. It does not authorize deployment, provider changes or data
writes.

## Worker and configuration

- Worker: `tuturuuu-cms` for production; the staging Worker name for
  staging.
- Hosts: only the root hosts `cms.tuturuuu.com` and `cms.tutur3u.com`. The
  `/cms` mount on `tuturuuu.com` is not served today: it is planned only after
  Tasks and Calendar reach the apex (the end state is `tuturuuu.com/cms`, with
  satellites moving to paths). The configuration rejects unknown hosts and
  disables Workers.dev and preview URLs. Source of truth:
  `apps/cms/start-bridge.config.ts` (`mountHosts: []`, `unknownHost: 'reject'`)
  and `apps/cms/src/runtime/root-host-policy.test.ts`, which asserts
  `https://tuturuuu.com/cms/...` returns 404.
- Build: `cd apps/cms && bun run build:cloudflare`.
- Static asset binding: `ASSETS`. Optional internal API origin variable:
  `INTERNAL_WEB_API_ORIGIN`. The build profile sets `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX`.
- Runtime secret names required by CMS: `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`,
  `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`. Abuse guard: service binding `ABUSE_GUARD` to `tuturuuu-abuse-guard`, secret `ABUSE_GUARD_KEY_PEPPER`, text variable `ABUSE_GUARD_FAMILIES=proxy`, and optional `ABUSE_GUARD_TIMEOUT_MS`. Upstash credentials are not required.
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` is a non-secret environment binding. Set secret
  values only in the protected runtime secret store; this page records names
  only.

## Smoke checks

After an authorized cutover, probe public deployment identity on the root host and
verify the native runtime header and expected source SHA:

```sh
curl -fsS -D - https://cms.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info
```

Run the existing isolated emitted-worker and cutover smoke checks before
publication:

```sh
(cd apps/cms && CI=true CI_SOURCE_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" bun run test:runtime)
node scripts/ci/cms-cutover-smoke.mjs
```

Confirm anonymous `/` redirects to `/login`, unknown hosts are rejected, and
the root-host build-info request returns the deployed identity.

## Rollback

Before routing changes, Rex records the immutable Vercel deployment ID and the
exact routes, custom domains and DNS records being replaced, plus the one-step
restore command and rollback owner. No deployment ID is recorded in this
repository, so Rex must capture it. Restore that routing to the prior deployment
immediately if smoke or the post-cutover watch regresses. Keep the deployment
available for the full release cycle.

## CMS caching and purge

Public CMS delivery and published assets are served by `apps/web` behind an edge
cache keyed on the per-workspace delivery version. The product rules live in
[Caching and publish visibility](/platform/features/external-project-studio#caching-and-publish-visibility);
this section is the operator procedure.

### Verify a HIT or MISS

Read the response headers on the public delivery route (replace the workspace id; no
credentials are needed for published content):

```sh
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null \
  "https://tuturuuu.com/api/v1/workspaces/<wsId>/external-projects/delivery" \
  | grep -i -E '^(HTTP|cache-control|etag|x-tuturuuu-delivery-)'
```

- `X-Tuturuuu-Delivery-Cache: MISS` on the first read after a version change, then
  `HIT` on repeats. `BYPASS` means the fence is on, the request was a preview, or the
  read was not eligible for the edge cache.
- `X-Tuturuuu-Delivery-Version` is the number the cache key is built from. It must
  equal the `version` returned by
  `GET /api/v1/workspaces/<wsId>/external-projects/delivery/version`.
- Send the returned `ETag` back as `If-None-Match`; a `304` with no body confirms
  revalidation. A preview read (`?preview=true`) must answer `private, no-store` and
  `BYPASS`. A `public` Cache-Control on a preview read is a defect: stop and escalate.
- Asset reads (`.../external-projects/assets/<assetId>?v=<digest>`) report the same
  cache header and carry `public, max-age=3600, s-maxage=86400` only for published
  digests.

### Bust the cache

- Normal edits need nothing: any content write (entries, blocks, assets, relations,
  field definitions, page versions, publish events, asset publication proofs, binding
  and template changes) bumps the workspace version in the same transaction, and the
  next read after the 2 second isolate memo misses and rebuilds.
- A manual bump goes only through a reviewed migration or an admin action. Never run
  ad-hoc SQL against production and never edit the version table by hand.
- `apps/cms-renderer` keys its rendered HTML on the delivery version as well, so a
  publish needs no `/__cms/purge` call. `POST /__cms/purge` with
  `{"scope":"workspace"}` and the site's purge token still rotates that site's HTML
  namespace when an operator must force a re-render.
- External apps that cache delivery compare
  `GET .../external-projects/delivery/version` and re-read delivery only when the
  number changed.

### Fence and rollback

- Fence: set `CMS_DELIVERY_EDGE_CACHE=0` on the web Worker and redeploy through the
  normal release path. Delivery and asset reads then answer `BYPASS` and rebuild on
  every request; the version endpoint and the editor are unaffected. Use it first when
  stale content is reported and `X-Tuturuuu-Delivery-Version` already matches the
  version endpoint.
- Rollback: revert the web commit that introduced the edge cache. The version table
  and its triggers are harmless if left in place, so the database needs no rollback.
- Cost bound: one primary-key read per workspace per isolate every 2 seconds on the
  version path and one row upsert per write statement. The Cache API adds no
  per-operation charge and no new Cloudflare binding.
